lead: The last housing estate built in Nou Barris before democracy, with metro line 3 at street level.
text: Its origin lies in the 18th-century farmhouse (masia) of Can Guineueta and in the district of Guineueta Vella, which after the Civil War filled up with shacks and small houses, with 250 homes without electricity or sewers. In the mid-1960s the project for the Ronda de Dalt doomed that settlement: the land was expropriated to build a housing estate and the farmhouse disappeared.

Community campaigning won the people of Guineueta Vella the right to live in the three thousand homes of the new neighbourhood, which opened in 1978. Today Canyelles occupies a hillside, with 6,906 inhabitants in 0.79 km² and a density of 8,742 inhabitants/km², considerably lower than that of Les Roquetes or La Guineueta, and it has Canyelles station on metro line 3. At 2,533 €/m² and 791 €/month, its prices are among the lowest in Nou Barris. If you are selling, the average sale price is 14% below the Nou Barris average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 203,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Nou Barris (8th of 13 by price). If you are investing, the average rent is in line with the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Blocks of a housing estate opened in 1978, on hillside streets.
